description:
FOUND s499g (probed perl 5.40.3 vs PCL at 53ca4e46).  `pcl -MData::Dumper sub/zero.pl` where zero.pl is `print "$0 ", __FILE__, " ", __LINE__, "\n";` prints `/tmp/pcl_NNN.pl /tmp/pcl_NNN.pl 2` where perl prints `sub/zero.pl sub/zero.pl 1`; with `use FindBin` the run DIES `Cannot find current script '/tmp/pcl_NNN.pl'` (the temp copy is unlinked before the run).  CAUSE: pcl's File+-M branch prepends the use-lines into a temp copy and hands THAT to pl2cl.  FIX SHAPE: tell pl2cl the as-given name (the preamble's $0 already comes from its source-file argument) and emit the -M lines on line 0 / via a #line directive, or have pl2cl take the -M list itself.  Until s499g the same branch also put the script's directory on @INC with -I (removed with #2442), which is not the fix for this.

=== DONE (s499j) ===
pcl -M: the use-lines go onto the script's FIRST code line of the temp copy (after the first =cut for a POD-first script), and pl2cl compiles it --as=<script as given>. $0, __FILE__, __LINE__, warn/die " at FILE line N." and FindBin identical to perl for sub/zero.pl run from elsewhere with -MData::Dumper (and -M with -e). NOT fixed: caller()'s file/line name the .lisp -- for EVERY program, not just -M (pre-existing, #233 family). Guards Pl/t/pcl-dash-m-01.t rows 8-9 (inverse-verified).
subject: `pcl -MMod script.pl`: $0, __FILE__ and line numbers name the TEMP copy pcl writes, so FindBin dies "Cannot find current script"
